events.definition: Something was made available to use or buy for the first time, or a new version of it was.
Two or more organisations agreed to work together, with neither buying the other.
One organisation bought another, or a controlling share of it.
An organisation raised money from investors, or was valued in the course of doing so.
An organisation committed money to build or expand physical capacity - a plant, a data centre, a power connection or the land for one.
An organisation reported its results for a trading period, or told the market what to expect from the next one.
A government, a regulator or a court acted on what an organisation may do, or moved to.
A study, a paper or a benchmark was published, stating a method and a result a reader could check.
Something broke, leaked or stopped working, and somebody outside the organisation was affected.

lenses.definition: The story turns on what the money spent on artificial intelligence bought.
The story turns on China - its government, its companies, or a decision another country has taken about it.
The story turns on semiconductors - who designs them, who makes them, the plants and machines that produce them, or who is allowed to buy them.
The story turns on what investors and traders did - a share price, an index, a bond yield, a valuation, or a market's reaction to something.
The story turns on goods or technology crossing a border, and on the tariffs, quotas, export controls or bans that meet them there.
The story turns on armed conflict - the fighting, the weapons, the people it displaces, or the talks to stop it.

verticals.definition: The story is mainly about artificial intelligence - the models, the people and companies building or selling them, the machines and data centres they run on, or the rules being written for them.
